title: Alfresco records no content audit trail until an administrator switches one on
content:
`repository.properties` ships `audit.enabled=true` alongside `audit.alfresco-access.enabled=false`. The first property is a decoy: it arms the auditing framework without producing any records. Alfresco's own documentation says so directly — *"enabling this property does not necessarily result in the generation of audit data"* — and elsewhere, *"The auditing system is disabled by default, as it has the potential to impact performance."*

The consequence is that a default Alfresco Community install has no content audit trail whatsoever. DoD 5015 auditing (`audit.dod5015.enabled=false`) and download auditing are off for the same reason.

This matters more than a missing feature would. An organisation that believes it has an audit trail because the config says `audit.enabled=true` has a governance gap it cannot see, and will discover it at the moment it needs the record.
description: audit.enabled=true only arms the framework; audit.alfresco-access.enabled is false by default, so a stock install generates no audit data at all.
